description:
## Why

A `pub fn` in production code reads as API. A future agent scanning the codebase
cannot tell that a helper exists only to let a test look inside, so it gets reused
and the test-only surface becomes load-bearing. The fix is to make the production
build not contain it at all.

## Signal

dead_code already proves no pub(crate)/pub(super)/private function is test-only: in a
non-test lib build such an item has zero callers and warns, and cargo build is clean
under -D warnings. The blind spot is fully-pub items, which the lint exempts as public
API. 47 of those have no non-test caller.

## The split (measured)

Integration tests in tests/ (aot_variadic_open, fixture_matrix, fz2_cli) compile
against the lib as an EXTERNAL crate, so they cannot see #[cfg(test)] items. That
divides the 47:

- 5 must stay pub -- consumed from tests/: fixture_matrix_paths_from_filename,
  parse_fixture_metadata, formula_totals, product_totals, functions. Leave them pub
  and name them as harness surface, or relocate the harness itself into tests/.
- 42 are consumed only by unit tests inside the lib and can move.

## The mechanic

All 42 are METHODS on production types (World::callsite_targets,
PublicTrace::events_named, Value::is_numeric, ...), not free functions, so they cannot
literally move into a test file. Move each into a `#[cfg(test)] impl` block on its own
type. That is strictly stronger than narrowing to pub(crate): the method does not
exist in a production build, so it cannot be reused by accident or on purpose, and
dead_code governs what remains. cfg(test) items stay visible to unit tests across
modules, so no test loses access.

## Not in this bucket: compile_root_jit

compile_root_jit has 0 production callers while its three sibling front doors ship
(run_root_interp 4, run_root_jit 2, compile_root_aot 1). That is not test scaffolding
-- it is either dead public API or a three-path parity gap. Decide it on its own
merits; do not silently cfg(test) a front door.

## Goal

Every fully-pub function either has a non-test consumer, or is named harness surface
for tests/, or lives behind cfg(test). After that the lint alone is a sufficient gate
and this scan never needs repeating.

## Origin

Found while merging main into fz-tfn/long-lived-recalculator (PR #118). The merge
applied the rule where it bore on a conflict: emitted_executables was deleted once
main removed its only consumer, and a test-only RootId import moved out of production
scope into the test module that uses it.
title: Move test-only helpers out of the production surface
